name: DotPagination
description: A row of round dots marking position in a carousel or slideshow. Knockout styling (white dots) — built for dark and media surfaces.

props.name: count
props.description: How many dots. The range is closed at five, so it is enumerable rather than open: Figma caps it with five Show Dot booleans (1–3 on by default) and the code clamps to the same 1–5. Values are strings because the defs schema types enum members that way; the code accepts either and parses. Figma has no single property for this — a component there cannot vary its child count, so the same decision is spelled five ways. One number is the API. See decision dp-count-booleans.

props.name: activeIndex
props.description: Zero-based index of the active dot, clamped to count. In Figma the equivalent is which child instance is set to State=active.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the nav landmark. Authored because the surrounding carousel should name itself.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Integration detail, not a design decision: receives the selected dot index. Omitting it leaves the dots as non-interactive indicators.

root.description: A nav landmark named by ariaLabel. Lays out inline so it can sit over media without reserving a row.

dot.description: One part, repeated 1–5 times — count decides how many. Figma names the instances .dot-1 … .dot-5 and builds each from an internal Dot component set; in code they share one class and differ only by data-state. Active dot takes color/content/knockout; the focus ring takes color/focus-ring/knockout.

keyboard.action: moves focus through the dots, one stop each
selects that slide when onSelect is wired

notes: Dots are real <button> elements inside a <nav> landmark — keyboard operable (2.1.1).
Active dot carries aria-current='true'; each dot has an aria-label naming its slide (4.1.2).
Focus ring uses focus-ring/knockout for visibility on the dark surfaces this component targets (2.4.7).
8px hit area is below the 24px target-size guideline (2.5.8 AA) — acceptable as an inline indicator, but pair with adjacent prev/next controls for primary navigation.
